notes.title: Dev Update #003: From dust to dominance
notes.content:
[h1]Introducing the new Material system[/h1][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27154671/356d839aed47a91f27c6ef044c9f5c90f7b0d157.png"][/img][/p][p]We have completely redesigned the materials into something tangible and should be easily understood during gameplay. We have introduced 4 materials that the player can find and collect during gameplay. Semiconductors, Metals, Minerals, and Volatiles.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27154671/2c882e88e8c5321f4a6182281ec1ca6a4318f5d4.png"][/img]Pilots can mine these materials in asteroid belts, collect them from destroyed ACE pods that have them onboard, or even trade for them. The stock ACE pod can carry up to 4 at a time, but more slots can be acquired at a [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/545840/view/542238020045111729"]Forge OASIS[/url].[/p][p][/p][h2]What do they do?[/h2][p]There are two main purposes of materials:[/p][p][/p][p]First and most important, they are still used for upgrades. You don’t strictly need them to upgrade, but you won’t have very much control over what upgrades you get without them. If you like a certain type of build, then you will want to be scavenging for these as much as possible.
[/p][p]Second, and new to Convicted Galaxy, is the ability to ‘consume’ materials during gameplay to help out in a pinch. Out of fuel? A volatile material can optionally be used to replenish your fuel. In a battle and need to use an advanced ability? A semiconductor can generate power cores. [/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27154671/62c72011dfc56bba8f89fed904e91881034e8251.png"][/img]We are still balancing the exact effects of these materials, but they certainly make cruising through asteroid belts a lot more meaningful. [/p][p][/p][h2]Theory behind the new design[/h2][p]The last build of Convicted Galaxy had an overly complex representation of rare materials. If you controlled a planet, you had access to the materials present on that planet. There were 16 materials categorized into 4 groups. [/p][p][/p][p]Some upgrades required a specific material, while others only needed a material from their group. We found that using the 4 material groups made upgrade interactions easier without reducing the overall mechanic functionality.[/p][p][/p][p]Additionally, we made the decision to make the materials a tangible pickup, rather than an abstract resource. This made it more exciting to seek out materials, and enabled new gameplay mechanics for us to experiment with. Overall, we were able to reduce complexity while improving gameplay.[/p]

Pilots can mine these materials in asteroid belts, collect them from destroyed ACE pods that have them onboard, or even trade for them.
The stock ACE pod can carry up to 4 at a time, but more slots can be acquired at a [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/545840/view/542238020045111729"]Forge OASIS[/url].
Second, and new to Convicted Galaxy, is the ability to ‘consume’ materials during gameplay to help out in a pinch.
Out of fuel? A volatile material can optionally be used to replenish your fuel.
In a battle and need to use an advanced ability? A semiconductor can generate power cores.

notes.title: Dev Update #002: Power Up at the OASIS
notes.content: [p]In any rogue-lite, one of the first things a player is going to look for is how to get stronger. We’ve tried a variety of progression mechanics throughout Convicted Galaxy’s development, and we’re very happy to arrive at what we are calling the “OASIS”, short for Operational Asset Synthesis and Integration Station, a significant overhaul of the ACE pod upgrade process![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27154671/647d41dd0432fd7e9a9ae224f7176a02291724b4.png"][/img]Prior to the dispersal of ACE pods into various solar systems, the ICF has scattered many specialized stations throughout the systems, the OASIS. Each stock ACE pod has a very minimal set of features. Every ACE pod is going to encounter their own unique struggles during their mission. To enhance their success, a pilot can visit an OASIS to outfit their ship with new functionality.[/p][p][/p][p]The OASIS utilizes an AI network to determine a suitable upgrade for the visiting ACE pod. Each OASIS can only be visited by an ACE pod once. Further upgrades must be obtained by seeking out additional OASIS.[/p][p][/p][p]Although an ACE pod is guaranteed a beneficial upgrade on every visit, it is in the best interest of the pilot to bring [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/545840/view/542238020045111731"]rare materials[/url] or ore along for more specialized and custom tailored upgrades. [/p][p][/p][p]There are two common variants: the Nexus, and the Forge.[/p][p][/p][h2]Nexus OASIS[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27154671/d7618ccb56e08b48920a88138bf1a3728de42283.png"][/img][/p][p]The Nexus OASIS will provide unique upgrades that can drastically change the capabilities of the ACE pod. These can include new abilities, new weaponry, and new passive functionalities. Each ACE pod is only permitted a single entry per Nexus and can acquire one upgrade in that visit. The Nexus does not utilize the more common ore that is collected. When entering a Nexus, pilots should bring rare materials for a better upgrade selection.[/p][p][/p][p]An ACE pod is guaranteed an upgrade on every visit to a Nexus, but if the pilot does not bring any rare materials for the on-station AI to work with, then the station will determine an upgrade for you. Nexus can be found in open space, often between planets.[/p][p][/p][h2]Forge OASIS[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27154671/40a003f6be7711f047f3957586d8adad565af893.png"][/img][/p][p]The Forge OASIS will provide linear upgrades to basic ACE pod stats such as hull integrity, shield capacity, thruster power, etc. Ore gathered from asteroids and dropped from other ACE pods are used to facilitate these upgrades. Notably, the Forge will always contain a cache to reimburse the pilot for at least one upgrade. [/p][p][/p][p]Like the Nexus, only one visit is allowed. However, the pilot can get as many upgrades as they can afford with their available ore. You can find these commonly in asteroid belts.[/p][p][/p][h2]Theory behind the new design[/h2][p]The old system of upgrading was based on experience and planetary control. It was cumbersome, hard to understand, and did not fit into the story or game flow well. We wanted to give the player the autonomy to build their ship, but the inspiration to explore and not spend too much time in the menus. We think the OASIS system will be exciting and tie various game elements together nicely.[/p][p][/p][h2]What’s next?[/h2][p]This post is the first in a series of posts introducing new content as we work toward a major update.[/p]

tags.feature: We’ve tried a variety of progression mechanics throughout Convicted Galaxy’s development, and we’re very happy to arrive at what we are calling the “OASIS”, short for Operational Asset Synthesis and Integration Station, a significant overhaul of the ACE pod upgrade process!

Each stock ACE pod has a very minimal set of features. Every ACE pod is going to encounter their own unique struggles during their mission. To enhance their success, a pilot can visit an OASIS to outfit their ship with new functionality.

The OASIS utilizes an AI network to determine a suitable upgrade for the visiting ACE pod. Each OASIS can only be visited by an ACE pod once. Further upgrades must be obtained by seeking out additional OASIS.

Although an ACE pod is guaranteed a beneficial upgrade on every visit, it is in the best interest of the pilot to bring [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/545840/view/542238020045111731"]rare materials[/url] or ore along for more specialized and custom tailored upgrades.

The Nexus OASIS will provide unique upgrades that can drastically change the capabilities of the ACE pod. These can include new abilities, new weaponry, and new passive functionalities. Each ACE pod is only permitted a single entry per Nexus and can acquire one upgrade in that visit. The Nexus does not utilize the more common ore that is collected. When entering a Nexus, pilots should bring rare materials for a better upgrade selection.

An ACE pod is guaranteed an upgrade on every visit to a Nexus, but if the pilot does not bring any rare materials for the on-station AI to work with, then the station will determine an upgrade for you. Nexus can be found in open space, often between planets.

The Forge OASIS will provide linear upgrades to basic ACE pod stats such as hull integrity, shield capacity, thruster power, etc. Ore gathered from asteroids and dropped from other ACE pods are used to facilitate these upgrades. Notably, the Forge will always contain a cache to reimburse the pilot for at least one upgrade.
Like the Nexus, only one visit is allowed. However, the pilot can get as many upgrades as they can afford with their available ore. You can find these commonly in asteroid belts.

The old system of upgrading was based on experience and planetary control. It was cumbersome, hard to understand, and did not fit into the story or game flow well. We wanted to give the player the autonomy to build their ship, but the inspiration to explore and not spend too much time in menus. We think the OASIS system will be exciting and tie various game elements together nicely.

notes.title: Dev Update #001: A new lens
notes.content:
Convicted Galaxy is about to get a whole lot better…

[h2]Core concept: refocused[/h2]
We started development of Convicted Galaxy with a loose story and a core principle of keeping gameplay fun. This was a good approach for making progress toward a fun experience fairly quickly. We developed and shared a product that, we believe, was and still is quite fun. However, we want to provide a fun, worthwhile, and complete experience.

In the past year, we have solidified early concepts and have been focusing all design decisions around a cohesive, story-centric idea. This focus has made it much more fun and compelling to design, develop, and implement parts of the game that need to be finished. We believe this will translate to the game experience, making Convicted Galaxy more cohesive and interesting to play while keeping the fun aspects that already exist. And of course, leading to a version 1.0.

[h2]Path forward[/h2]
We are still a ways out from pushing a new build to the beta channel for open testing. Even though we have accomplished a lot of new work, there are some core features which need to be finished before we will feel ready for wide scale playtesting.

In the coming months, we plan to share Dev Updates on a regular basis, highlighting new content that will be available in the next build of Convicted Galaxy.

[h2]Upcoming features[/h2]
A sneak peek of some features that we have implemented and are still testing out:

[list]
[*] OASIS (upgrade) stations
[*] New ACE pod (your spaceship) design
[*] New Upgrades and Abilities
[*] Collectible materials
[*] Galactic phenomena to encounter
[*] Reworked audio assets
[*] Additional music tracks
[*] Interactive NPC and faction behavior
[/list]

Stay tuned!

notes.title: New weapons, solar system styles, and weapons HUD - v0.5.0
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/2bb8949d8042e06694a65da8323f6ba250c93a3c.gif[/img]
[h1]Improvements[/h1]
[b]New Weapons[/b]
Two new weapons have been added to your arsenal, the laser and mine secondary weapons. With the new change, hull types will also determine the secondary weapons you will receive. 
[list]
[*]Combat (Drone) hull -> Missiles
[*]Power (Gravity) hull -> Mines
[*]Speed (Decoy) hull -> Lasers
[*]Utility (EMP) hull -> No Secondary
[/list]
Stacking hull types will accumulate secondary weapons (just like abilities), allowing you to switch between them as you please. There is also an automated check to reset your controls to default so that you will get the new action mappings for switching weapons and build options. If you miss the option, go into the controls settings and set them to default or re-map the new controls related to the new actions for switching weapons and build options.

[b]Solar System Styles and Lighting[/b]
Quite a few visual improvements have been made, including additional solar system styles and lighting. Each system will now feel much more unique.[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/4158103c648eb9aa0000096309f0ccca4ead575c.gif[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/9cc844d522568b38437d050a512234f765b65846.gif[/img][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/9ccf2848ffc985364d0166a0b3583307d7ef2d3b.gif[/img]

[b]Inner Weapons HUD[/b]
A new inner HUD has been added to quickly notify you of your ability and weapon status. Below are a few images to help you get started until we fully flesh it out with icons.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/5d37f7eb6acbe333366921cb2ec11a86cf836fbc.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/cdf93075a55e87de4a195c7701e1ca7532e7ec72.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/c92e996e69ec2c70db30004a043e832d22a463fc.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/56af56ed573e6505efa0dc9ff7e10047505cbf28.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/a6084f17c5c5772dd2f4f043d0c12168592b4ebe.png[/img]

[b]And a lot more...[/b]

[b]Additionally[/b], we have fixed an issue that seemed to have come up when we added the OS X 32-bit build. Thanks to everyone who pointed out the issue and help resolve it! If you are unable to download the game, please let us know, as the issue should be solved.

[h1]Patch Notes[/h1]
As always, you can find the complete release notes here:
http://www.convictedgalaxy.com/releasenotes

Enjoy and let us know what you think!

notes.title: Friendly AI and beyond - v0.4.0
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/ec97275b17c6961281ecc19e2c8f574f18c31e90.gif[/img]
[h1]Improvements[/h1]
We've added friendly AI ships! Put the pilots you rescue to work. Build fighter ships like yours for them to use. Once constructed at a friendly station, the friendly AI fighters will follow you around and help you collect resources, defend your stations and assault the enemies. 

For now, you build a friendly AI fighter at a level 3 upgraded station with 600 scrap and a rescued ICF pilot. You can monitor their health and upgrades they have chosen in the new squad HUD. Go check it out!

A few more quick changes I want to note:
[list]
[*]All ships cruise speeds have been reduced. Think before just cruising off into open space.
[*]Lock-on missiles are no longer standard. You will start with a dumb fire missile just like the enemy AI. You can get the homing upgrade under the combat hull if you need it, but it will reduce the damage done by your missiles.
[*]All small (non-Frigate) ships can now use tethers. Stay away from enemies when your shields are down!
[/list]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/40f8a2b134308311445473af0f61b566c10989df.png[/img]
[h1]Patch Notes[/h1]
As always, you can find the release notes here:
http://www.convictedgalaxy.com/releasenotes

Enjoy and let us know what you think!

notes.title: OSX 32-bit Now Available
notes.content:
[h1]Unable to Install? (0 kb to download?)[/h1]
We have seen a few anonymous comments about purchasers who were unable to download the game (showing a download of 0 kb). [b][u]We would love to know more about your computer specs if this is you![/u][/b] All builds have been tested on our end and have files, with one exception, 32-bit OSX. 

[h1]A Universal OSX Build is Now Standard[/h1]
Prior to now, there has not been a 32-bit OSX version due to possible performance issues with older hardware that is unable to run 64-bit OSX. We believed that Steam would not allow 32-bit OSX users to purchase the game. However, this is the only way that purchasers may be having this issue, to our knowledge. As of today, the Universal OSX build will be standard to allow either 32-bit or 64-bit OSX to run Convicted Galaxy.

We hope this solves the issue, if you have any issues with the game, please let us know via the discussion board or email!

Thanks and Enjoy!

tags.feature: As of today, the Universal OSX build will be standard to allow either 32-bit or 64-bit OSX to run Convicted Galaxy.

notes.content:

v0.3.4 is incoming with a lot of new changes. Frigate class ships, Ice asteroids, additional planet variations and more!

We don't expect this to impact too many users, and it will be well worth all the new goodies. We will post again once the update goes live later today :)

notes.title: Controller Support - v0.3.1
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154671/d5acda53be73eec38fe73b2a6f66f6a59aab1324.png[/img]

[h1]Controller Support[/h1]
Our first update to Steam Early Access is primarily introducing controller support. Controller support will be an ongoing task, so please be patient and let us know if you have any issues. Most of our testing has been done with PS4 and XboxOne controllers, although it should work with most controllers.

Please let us know if there are any issues or any suggestions on additional mappings in the discussions page:
http://steamcommunity.com/app/545840/discussions/ 

Along with a few visual changes to the HUD, we have also done some minor balancing changes to damage done by lasers in particular.

[h1]Patch Notes[/h1]
As always, you can find the release notes here:
http://www.convictedgalaxy.com/releasenotes

[h1]What's next?[/h1]
Next up, we will be looking to make some more visual and mechanic implementations, such as more visual changes when upgrading stations or ships and the implementation of more satellite types.
